name: Milestone 5 accepted eval baseline
purpose: Regression baseline for the live evaluation gate. This is not a perfection target; it is the committed quality floor. Pull requests may improve it, but may not silently drop below it or introduce new failed question IDs.

accepted_failures.reason: The answer lives in the 14 CFR 61.23(d) duration table, but the parsed chunk text only contains the table lead-in. Fixing this belongs in PDF table extraction/re-chunking, not generation.
The Victor airway class and width facts span multiple AIM chunks. v1 deliberately avoids stitching a synthesized answer across several excerpts.
Class C VFR weather minimums are a list-style answer; v1 favors one concise source excerpt over exhaustive synthesis.
Transponder requirements are spread across several conditions; v1 may answer from the strongest excerpt without listing every condition.
Required aircraft inspections span several sections. v1 cites the annual inspection source rather than synthesizing an exhaustive checklist across sections.
Required aircraft documents can require more than one supported item; current v1 may omit one checklist item while preserving citation trust.
Class B entry requirements are a multi-item checklist; current v1 may answer the clearance requirement without every related equipment item.
PIC document carriage spans several required documents; current v1 may omit one item rather than synthesize beyond one excerpt.
The required duration facts are in a PDF table that is not reliably present in parsed chunk text.
Private pilot aeronautical experience is a long requirements list; current v1 answers can be partial under the single-excerpt design.
The current answer is concise and cited but can miss one applicability detail. This is tracked as completeness behavior, not citation trust.
The expected Class E and airway-width facts live in different AIM chunks, conflicting with the v1 single-excerpt verification model.
Hypoxia symptoms and types are a broad list-style answer; current v1 may answer symptoms without exhaustively naming every type.
The accepted citation is AIM 4-3-3, but the expected 45-degree entry phrasing is not cleanly supported by that chunk's text. Current v1 prioritizes the cited source text.
Runway holding-position markings include shape, side, and clearance meaning; current v1 can be correct but non-exhaustive.
